strongest_objection: The mechanisms hold; the illustrative cases do not, and in six items the author's own case list contains a case the item's own discriminator excludes, so the discriminator is blurred exactly where the sharpening check should have bitten. The worst is Countercyclical hand, which declares that 'the sign of the correlation is the whole mechanism' and then leads with the funeral player and the storm-repair builder, whose second weather is uncorrelated with the first trade's, not opposed to it: that is the pool-of-one the author's boundary case rules out as 'a second exposure'. The same fault recurs: the taxi medallion in Hiring hall is sold with the seller's years in it and so is property, not a queue that zeroes on leaving; the cook in Passport trade has no registry; the prison in Berth takes the exit right rather than buying it, which the boundary claim on floors held by force excludes, and the residency's exit price falls with every year rather than rising; the indenture in Advance against the crop has a fixed term that clears, the opposite of a debt the creditor wants never cleared; and the squatter in Plot that must be tended, once the claim ripens into title, holds property that keeps while unused. One price clause is wrong on the map's own logic: Roost ledger says standing on it 'costs nothing', but a meal received in a reciprocal ledger is a meal owed and draws the balance down, so the roost is the one floor both fed and spent by use, which is a sharper reading than the author's. Seriation misplaces Countercyclical hand after the hinge among floors indifferent to use when its own text says it is kept by fair-weather practice. Two edges into Prove the fall assert as general what is true only of tests that count cash and count the home: many means tests disregard the primary residence, and some, like a rule that reckons in-kind support, count a bed and a meal as income, which breaks the Kin policy edge's antecedent as written. None of this reaches the type or the axis, which survived every case I threw at them.

items.item: Plot that must be tended: a right to feed oneself outside any wage, as the allotment, the grazing right on the common, the village fishing berth, the squatter's occupation, keeps a floor under food that no employer can remove, and lapses with non-use, since commons rights, allotments, and adverse possession all require continuous occupation; the floor conserves calories and a place, is paid for in fair-weather labour the wage could have bought better, and standing on it costs mobility, since the plot cannot come with you; not property, which keeps while unused, but a floor that exists only by being stood on.
items.why: The legal generalization 'commons rights, allotments, and adverse possession all require continuous occupation' is asserted as fact and is wrong for the squatter: continuous possession is needed to acquire title, and once acquired the title is property that keeps while unused, which the item's own discriminator excludes. Customary rights are presumed abandoned only after long disuse, not on a missed season. The mechanism, a right that exists only by being stood on, is intact.
items.repair: Plot that must be tended: a right to feed oneself outside any wage, as the allotment, the grazing right on the common, the village fishing berth, the squatter's occupation, keeps a floor under food that no employer can remove, and lapses with non-use, since the allotment tenancy is ended for non-cultivation, the customary right is presumed abandoned after long disuse, and the squatter's claim exists only while in possession, and once that claim ripens into title it is property and leaves the map; the floor conserves calories and a place, is paid for in fair-weather labour the wage could have bought better, and standing on it costs mobility, since the plot cannot come with you; not property, which keeps while unused, but a floor that exists only by being stood on.

items.item: Roost ledger: a floor sized by one's own giving history, as vampire bats that fail to feed for two nights are fed by roost-mates who regurgitate blood, and are fed in proportion to what they themselves gave when fat, the ledger living in the recipients' memory; the floor conserves a night's meal, is paid by past recipients who remember, and standing on it costs nothing except that it is only there for those who paid out when they could, so the stingy have none; observed in bats, analytical in people, as the freelancer fed by those she once passed work to; not Burial club, whose contributions are fixed and whose ledger is a book, since here the floor strengthens with giving.
items.why: 'Standing on it costs nothing' contradicts the ledger the item describes: in a reciprocal ledger the meal received is the meal owed, and the balance that sized the floor is drawn down by the draw. Read correctly, the roost is the one floor on the map that use both feeds (giving) and spends (taking), which is stranger and more exact than the author's 'costs nothing' and belongs at the kept-by-use pole for that reason. 'In proportion' also overstates the observed result, which is that bats feed most those who fed them; modality is otherwise honestly marked.
items.repair: Roost ledger: a floor sized by one's own giving history, as vampire bats that fail to feed for two nights are fed by roost-mates who regurgitate blood, and are fed most by those they themselves fed when fat, the ledger living in the recipients' memory; the floor conserves a night's meal, is paid by past recipients who remember, and standing on it costs the ledger itself, since a meal taken is a meal owed and the balance that sized the floor is drawn down by the draw, so this floor is fed by giving and spent by taking and is only there for those who paid out when they could, and the stingy have none; observed in bats, analytical in people, as the freelancer fed by those she once passed work to; not Burial club, whose contributions are fixed and whose ledger is a book, since here the floor strengthens with giving.

items.item: Hiring hall: a guild or union that rations work by a queue, as the longshore hiring hall, the musicians' local, the taxi medallion, the licensed trade with a fixed number of seats, keeps a floor under access to work rather than under work itself; the floor conserves a place in line, is paid by the excluded who would take the work cheaper and by dues, and standing on it costs the queue itself, since seniority counts continuous presence and the better job elsewhere zeroes it, so the floor accrues by staying and is forfeited by the one move a rising member wants; not a union wage, which is a price, but a ration.
items.why: The taxi medallion and the fixed-seat licensed trade are sold, with the holder's years priced into the sale, so leaving does not zero them; they are property, which the map's type rules out, not a queue that counts presence. The hall and the local are the true cases; the union out-of-work book is a third. Naming the medallion as the excluded neighbour turns the slip into a discriminator.
items.repair: Hiring hall: a guild or union that rations work by a queue, as the longshore hiring hall, the musicians' local, the electricians' out-of-work book, keeps a floor under access to work rather than under work itself; the floor conserves a place in line, is paid by the excluded who would take the work cheaper and by dues, and standing on it costs the queue itself, since seniority counts continuous presence and the better job elsewhere zeroes it, so the floor accrues by staying and is forfeited by the one move a rising member wants; not a union wage, which is a price, but a ration, and not the taxi medallion or the notary's seat, which are sold with the seller's years in them and so are property.

items.item: Passport trade: a skill whose registry is honoured in any town, as the nurse, the welder, the electrician, the cook, keeps a floor under employability at the trade's local wage; the floor conserves the registry entry and not the skill, since a stranger hires the licence, is paid in training years and in hours logged to keep the licence from lapsing, and standing on it costs a re-registration, since the market reads you at the level you last worked, so the architect who drafts for two years is a draftsman to the next employer; adds to runway-illusions' Any-town skill, which counts the clock, and status-conversions' Staleness discount, which counts the lapse, the price of the step down; not the hands, which keep, but the entry, which must be used to keep.
items.why: The cook has no registry, so the item's own mechanism, 'a stranger hires the licence', does not apply; the cook's floor is runway-illusions' Any-town skill alone. This is also the item nearest to duplicating existing members, and its floor-specific residue (the entry that must be used to keep) is real but thin; naming the cook as the nonmember makes that residue visible.
items.repair: Passport trade: a skill whose registry is honoured in any town, as the nurse, the welder, the electrician, the pilot, keeps a floor under employability at the trade's local wage; the floor conserves the registry entry and not the skill, since a stranger hires the licence, is paid in training years and in hours logged to keep the licence from lapsing, and standing on it costs a re-registration, since the market reads you at the level you last worked, so the architect who drafts for two years is a draftsman to the next employer; adds to runway-illusions' Any-town skill, which counts the clock, and status-conversions' Staleness discount, which counts the lapse, the price of the step down; not the hands, which keep, but the entry, which must be used to keep, and not the cook, whose skill travels without a registry and so is Any-town skill alone.

items.item: Kept on call: a retainer that pays to keep you available is a floor that is really an option someone else holds, as the client who pays a monthly fee for first call on a lawyer, a plumber, a designer; the floor conserves a monthly minimum, is paid by the client as the premium on your time, and standing on it costs the better work, since the option is exercised exactly when you are busiest, and the floor holds only under light use: never called, it is cancelled at renewal as waste, always called, it is a job at their rate; not a salary, since nothing is owed for the hours, and not a job, since the trigger is in another hand.
items.why: 'The option is exercised exactly when you are busiest' asserts a correlation the mechanism does not supply; a first-call retainer is exercised when the client needs you, which need not track your load. The real price is that the trigger takes no account of your load, which the item's last clause already says. One word of modality.
items.repair: Kept on call: a retainer that pays to keep you available is a floor that is really an option someone else holds, as the client who pays a monthly fee for first call on a lawyer, a plumber, a designer; the floor conserves a monthly minimum, is paid by the client as the premium on your time, and standing on it costs the better work, since the option can be exercised at the moment you are busiest and takes no account of it, and the floor holds only under light use: never called, it is cancelled at renewal as waste, always called, it is a job at their rate; not a salary, since nothing is owed for the hours, and not a job, since the trigger is in another hand.

items.item: Countercyclical hand: a second trade whose demand rises in the weather that kills the first, as the session player who plays funerals, the builder who does insurance repairs, the bankruptcy lawyer, the pawnbroker, the bartender in a bust; the floor conserves income in bad weather, is paid by others' bad weather and by the fair-weather idleness of keeping the hand in, and standing on it costs the good-weather income the upkeep forgoes; not a side income, since the sign of the correlation is the whole mechanism, and a second source that fails with the first is a second exposure, as runway-illusions' Receivable from the dying shows from the other side of the sheet.
items.why: The item says the sign of the correlation is the whole mechanism, then leads with two cases whose correlation is zero: funerals do not rise in a bust and storms do not track the building cycle. Those are a pool of one, the diversification the author's own boundary case calls 'a second exposure', and Burial club's correlation condition governs them. Only the bankruptcy lawyer and the pawnbroker are countercyclical as written. Replaced with cases whose demand actually rises when the first trade's falls and named the excluded pair as the nonmember.
items.repair: Countercyclical hand: a second trade whose demand rises in the weather that kills the first, as the bankruptcy lawyer, the pawnbroker, the repossession agent, the auctioneer of failed stock, the discount grocer in a bust; the floor conserves income in bad weather, is paid by others' bad weather and by the fair-weather idleness of keeping the hand in, and standing on it costs the good-weather income the upkeep forgoes; not a side income, since the sign of the correlation is the whole mechanism, and a second source that fails with the first is a second exposure, as runway-illusions' Receivable from the dying shows from the other side of the sheet; and not the funeral player or the storm-repair builder, whose second weather is merely a different weather, a pool of one under Burial club's condition and not a hand that rises when the first falls.

items.item: Burial club: a pool of peers whose failures are uncorrelated, as the burial society, the rotating credit circle, the friendly society, the crew's kitty, keeps a floor under a lump at one's turn; the floor conserves the lump, is paid by members in advance and enforced by shame among equals, and standing on it costs the obligation to keep paying at others' turns after one's own failure, and the pool dies in the weather that fails everyone at once, as the village whose harvest is one harvest; adds to cooperation-mechanisms' insurance pools and joint liability the correlation condition and the premium that continues after the claim; not kin, whose premium comes after and whose enforcement is rank.
items.why: Tested as the author's left neighbour and separately against Kin policy; both separations hold (fixed dues versus giving history; premium before under shame versus premium after under rank). One wrinkle noted, not repaired: the handle's own case, the burial society, is the one member of its list whose 'failure' is death, so its price clause, the obligation to keep paying after one's own turn, belongs to the rotating circle and the friendly society rather than to the burial club that names the item.

items.item: Berth: an institution that buys the exit right, as the monastery, the army, the ship's articles, the prison, the hospital residency, the company town, keeps a floor under the whole person, bed, food, order, and rank; the floor conserves the person and not the income, is paid by the institution because it buys the exit option cheaply from someone at their lowest, and standing on it costs the exit, whose price rises with every year, since the sailor of twenty years cannot be a landsman and the pension vests in the year the walls are highest; the ship's articles bind both ways, the master to feed and the hand to stay, so this floor is enforced against its payer too; not a job, which does not own the evenings.
items.why: The prison does not buy the exit right cheaply from someone at their lowest; it takes it, which is a floor held by force and outside the map by the author's own boundary claim. The hospital residency has a fixed term and the exit price falls with every year served, the reverse of the mechanism. Both replaced; both named as the excluded neighbours, which sharpens what 'buys' means.
items.repair: Berth: an institution that buys the exit right, as the monastery, the army, the ship's articles, the company town, the live-in post, keeps a floor under the whole person, bed, food, order, and rank; the floor conserves the person and not the income, is paid by the institution because it buys the exit option cheaply from someone at their lowest, and standing on it costs the exit, whose price rises with every year, since the sailor of twenty years cannot be a landsman and the pension vests in the year the walls are highest; the ship's articles bind both ways, the master to feed and the hand to stay, so this floor is enforced against its payer too; not a job, which does not own the evenings, not the prison, which takes the exit right instead of buying it, and not the residency, whose exit price falls with every year served.

items.item: Advance against the crop: a debt that converts into a claim on future labour, as the sharecropper's advance of seed and food against the harvest, the indenture, the company store's tab, the boat-owner who advances the fisherman's season; the floor conserves calories now, is paid by the future, and standing on it costs the future, since the creditor profits from the debt continuing and keeps the books, so the floor deepens with each use and inverts into a keeper; the oldest floor on the map; not Creditor's chair, where the creditor's interest turned to your success.
items.why: The indenture has a fixed term that clears, so it is a debt with a date, a price rather than a floor the creditor wants never cleared; it contradicts the item's mechanism. Replaced with a debt-bonded case that has the rolling shape, and the indenture named as the nonmember.
items.repair: Advance against the crop: a debt that converts into a claim on future labour, as the sharecropper's advance of seed and food against the harvest, the company store's tab, the boat-owner who advances the fisherman's season, the kiln-owner's loan against the season's bricks; the floor conserves calories now, is paid by the future, and standing on it costs the future, since the creditor profits from the debt continuing and keeps the books, so the floor deepens with each use and inverts into a keeper; the oldest floor on the map; not Creditor's chair, where the creditor's interest turned to your success, and not the indenture, whose term is fixed and clears, since a debt with a date is a price and this floor has none.

items.item: Prove the fall: a means-tested floor is reachable only by proving no other floor exists, as unemployment assistance with an asset test, the parish relief, the hardship fund; the floor conserves a cash minimum, is paid by the taxpayer or the pool, and standing on it costs the other floors first, since the test counts the roof's equity and the savings and demands they be spent, and then the record of having stood there; a floor that is a wall in front of the others; not insurance, since the claim is not a premium paid but a state proven; invisible while floors were counted side by side.
items.why: 'The test counts the roof's equity' is asserted as the mechanism when many means tests disregard the primary residence, and some count a bed and board from kin as income; the edge into this item is conditional but the item is not. The wall's height is set by what the test can see, which is the sharper claim and the one the map's edges actually depend on.
items.repair: Prove the fall: a means-tested floor is reachable only by proving no other floor exists, as unemployment assistance with an asset test, the parish relief, the hardship fund; the floor conserves a cash minimum, is paid by the taxpayer or the pool, and standing on it costs the other floors first, since the test counts the savings, and where its rule reaches them the roof's equity and the family's bed and board, and demands they be spent, and then the record of having stood there; a floor that is a wall in front of the others, whose height is set by what the test can see; not insurance, since the claim is not a premium paid but a state proven; invisible while floors were counted side by side.

items.item: Unused door: a right to be somewhere else, as the second passport, the ancestral citizenship, the right of return, the village that must take you back, keeps a floor under standing here, since every counterparty who knows of the door prices the negotiation as if you might use it; the floor conserves the bargaining position, is paid by the second state's or the ancestor's reasons, and standing on it costs standing at home, since the emigrant loses the hall's queue and the one who used the second passport is suspect to both states, and some doors close on use, as the state that strips citizenship for taking another; worth most while unused; not a place to go, which is Berth or Plot, but a right the counterparty knows you have.
items.why: Tested against the type's trigger, 'when the main source fails': the door floors standing in every negotiation, not only after a fall, and it is closer to a bargaining position than to a catch. It stays because the type names standing as well as income, because the counterparty's pricing of the door is a real second hand, and because it separates from Uncalled favour by acting while unused and by being known, where the favour acts only when called. Kept with that reading on the record.

items.item: Accident only: a priced floor from a stranger, as the disability policy, the income-protection policy, the crop insurance, pays in cash and leaves no debt in standing, because the premium was paid before the fall; the floor conserves cash, is paid by the premium and by the other policyholders whose falls did not come, and standing on it costs the exclusions and the repricing, since the stranger covers what happened to you and refuses what you did, the quit, the risk you chose, the pre-existing, and raises the premium after the claim; not Prove the fall, which covers the chosen fall after proof and a wait, and not kin, who cover both at a price in rank.
items.why: Plainest item on the map, but it carries the indifferent pole and is separated from Prove the fall (state proven versus premium paid) and Kin policy (the chosen fall covered at a price in rank). One modality nit left in place: 'raises the premium after the claim' is true of property and motor cover and not of non-cancellable disability policies, which refuse renewal or reprice at term instead.

neighbor_test.left: Hiring hall: a guild or union that rations work by a queue, as the longshore hiring hall, the musicians' local, the taxi medallion, the licensed trade with a fixed number of seats, keeps a floor under access to work rather than under work itself; the floor conserves a place in line, is paid by the excluded who would take the work cheaper and by dues, and standing on it costs the queue itself, since seniority counts continuous presence and the better job elsewhere zeroes it, so the floor accrues by staying and is forfeited by the one move a rising member wants; not a union wage, which is a price, but a ration.
neighbor_test.right: Passport trade: a skill whose registry is honoured in any town, as the nurse, the welder, the electrician, the cook, keeps a floor under employability at the trade's local wage; the floor conserves the registry entry and not the skill, since a stranger hires the licence, is paid in training years and in hours logged to keep the licence from lapsing, and standing on it costs a re-registration, since the market reads you at the level you last worked, so the architect who drafts for two years is a draftsman to the next employer; adds to runway-illusions' Any-town skill, which counts the clock, and status-conversions' Staleness discount, which counts the lapse, the price of the step down; not the hands, which keep, but the entry, which must be used to keep.
neighbor_test.separating_case: An electrician with fifteen years on the local's out-of-work book and a state licence loses her main contractor. If she stays, the book floors her: her place in line yields the next call, at the hall's rationed quantity. If she takes the better job two states away, the book zeroes on the day she leaves, while the licence is honoured on reciprocity and floors her employability at the new town's rate but gives her no place in any line. The hall's floor is forfeited by the move and the trade's floor is what survives it; one rations quantity by presence, the other floors price by registry, and the same person stands on both until the move tells her which was which. They do not collapse.

boundary_case: The freezer full of venison, or the prepper's pantry: tempting because it is literally 'a floor under food that no employer can remove', the phrase Plot that must be tended uses. Ruled out: no second hand is on it and its decay is indifferent to use, since it rots whether or not it is eaten, so it is the cash pile in calories and the map sees it only as what Plot produces. The ruling sharpens Plot, whose floor is the right and not the produce. A second try, the author's own open seed, the collateralised credit line: it has a hand on it (the bank's) but fails the type at the trigger clause, since it is withdrawn at the fall it would be needed for; it is out not for lacking a hand but for not being there when the main source fails, which makes it the shape of a non-floor the type's trigger already names.

seriation.note: The axis has real endpoints and the two named adjacencies teach: Berth to Roof as piggy bank is the same object as floor and wall, and Advance to Kin policy separates two never-clearing debts by why they never clear. One misplacement: Countercyclical hand sits after Kept on call among the floors indifferent to use, but its own text says it is kept by fair-weather practice, which is Passport trade's rule; standing on it in a bust keeps the hand in. It belongs between Passport trade and Kept on call, so the route reads Passport trade (kept by hours logged) to Countercyclical hand (kept by practice in fair weather, used in foul) to Kept on call (kept only by light use), and the hinge is unchanged. With the Roost repair the first pole also reads better: the roost is fed by giving and spent by taking, which is why it sits second and not first.

edges.why: The antecedent is honestly conditional and the incompatibility is real where it holds. The tail, 'only what is on the bailiff's list is invisible to the test', conflates two lists: bankruptcy exemptions and means-test disregards are written by different laws and often disagree, so a roof can be safe from the creditor and fatal to the claim, or the reverse. Tested Roof and Tools the bailiff cannot take as neighbours on this point: they separate (forced saving versus legislated shield; the roof is where they coincide), and the edge is where the coincidence was mistaken for identity.
edges.repair_label: If the state's floor is means-tested and the test counts the equity behind the roof, then the roof must be sold or borrowed against before the state's floor opens, so the two cannot both be kept: reaching one requires destroying the other; and what the test does not count is the test's own list, not the bailiff's, so a roof can be safe from the creditor and fatal to the claim, or the reverse, depending on which list the jurisdiction wrote.

edges.why: The passage is plausible but the carrier is unstated and the direction of the residual favour is ambiguous: a client who paid a year for nothing may feel owed rather than kept, in which case the favour runs the other way and the passage fails. Making the antecedent the amicable lapse ('anytime' rather than rupture) gives the edge a condition that can fail and names who holds the favour.
edges.repair_label: If the retainer lapses for want of calls and is let go with an 'anytime' rather than a rupture, what remains is the client's sense of having been kept, an uncalled favour of unknown size held by the one who was on call, so the floor that lived by light use decays into the floor that dies by the first call; the passage runs one way, since a called favour does not become a retainer, and it fails where the client leaves feeling they paid for nothing, since then the favour is owed the other way.

edges.from_handle: Kin policy, premium after the claim
edges.why: 'If kin pay in kind, the means test sees no cash' is false for tests that reckon in-kind support and maintenance as income, where a free bed and board reduce the benefit; the claim that the unit decides is right only against a test that reads cash alone. Adding the test's unit to the antecedent keeps the mechanism and makes it a claim that can fail.
edges.repair_label: If the test reads only cash and kin pay in kind, the test sees nothing and both floors hold; if kin pay in cash, or the test reckons a bed and a meal as income, as a rule that counts in-kind support does, the state's floor closes; so whether the two floors can be stood on together is decided by the unit the family pays in set against the unit the test reads, and not by how much is given.

edges.why: A real fork with a failing antecedent, and it has a third tine the map does not draw: if the creditor can take neither a share nor your labour, the debt discharges onto the bailiff's list, so Tools the bailiff cannot take is the fork's third branch. Left as a seed rather than an edge.

modality_problems: Plot that must be tended states as law that commons rights, allotments, and adverse possession all lapse with non-use; only the allotment tenancy does so on a season's neglect, customary rights lapse by presumed abandonment after long disuse, and a completed adverse possession is property that keeps while unused (repaired).

Roost ledger's 'fed in proportion to what they themselves gave' overstates the observed finding, which is that bats feed most those who fed them; and 'standing on it costs nothing' is wrong for a reciprocal ledger (repaired).
Kept on call asserts the option 'is exercised exactly when you are busiest', a correlation the mechanism does not supply (repaired to 'can be').
Countercyclical hand's funeral and storm-repair cases are uncorrelated with the first trade's weather, not countercyclical, and 'the bartender in a bust' is a contested folk claim (repaired).
Berth's prison is a floor held by force, excluded by the map's own boundary claim; the residency's exit price falls with time (repaired).
Advance against the crop's indenture has a fixed clearing term, contrary to the item's mechanism (repaired).

Prove the fall and two edges into it assert that the means test counts the roof's equity and sees no in-kind support; both are true of some tests and false of others, and the edges' whole claim depends on which (repaired in item and labels).
Accident only's 'raises the premium after the claim' does not hold for non-cancellable disability cover (noted, kept).
Sponsor's promise cites Studebaker as documented history; that is correct (the 1963 plant closure and pension default that led to ERISA) and is left as is.
duplication: none as a whole map; no grown list is about floors. Adjacencies are declared and add something: Burial club adds the correlation condition to cooperation-mechanisms' pools; Uncalled favour adds the collapse rule to exchange-ontologies' Obligation futures and pivot-invariants' war chest of favours; Kin policy is the payout side of runway-illusions' Lien of blood. Passport trade is the one item near duplication (runway-illusions' Any-town skill plus status-conversions' Staleness discount); its residue, the registry entry that must be used to keep, is thin but real, and the repair names the cook as the case that belongs to Any-town skill alone.
best_unresolved_seed: Which hands can see which floors. Three of the map's edges turn on visibility rather than size: the means test sees the roof in one jurisdiction and not another, sees kin's cash but not kin's bed under one rule and both under another, and the bailiff's list and the test's disregard list are two lists that need not agree. The roost ledger is visible to no test at all; the uncalled favour is invisible until called. A matrix of each floor's legibility to the gatekeeper of every other floor, floor by floor and jurisdiction by jurisdiction, would let an operator infer which floors can be stood on together, which is the question the map's incompatibility edges answer only pairwise; it connects to the author's next crossfield opening on means tests as witness architectures, and to the fork's third tine, where a debt no creditor can convert discharges onto the bailiff's list.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing nine items whose illustrative cases broke their own discriminators or misstated a price, moving Countercyclical hand among the floors kept by use, and relabeling three edges whose antecedents held only for means tests that read cash alone.
